title: Degree-3 Polynomial Features with a Scaled Linear Regression Pipeline
description: Expand X into [x, x^2, x^3] with PolynomialFeatures(degree=3, include_bias=False), split using the supplied ratio, fit a StandardScaler + LinearRegression pipeline, and plot y_pred vs. y_test.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Create `poly = PolynomialFeatures(degree=3, include_bias=False)` and transform the single-column feature matrix `X` into `X_poly` with columns `[x, x^2, x^3]`. Split `(X_poly, y)` into train and test sets using the supplied ratio.

Build `model = Pipeline([("scaler", StandardScaler()), ("linreg", LinearRegression())])`, fit on `(X_train, y_train)`, predict `y_pred = model.predict(X_test)`, and print `Test RMSE: 0.6429365959079092` and `Test R^2: 0.8985803002973695`.

Look at lines 3-4 and 10-13: `include_bias=False` omits the constant `1` column from `X_poly` because `LinearRegression()` fits its own intercept, and `StandardScaler()` normalizes `x`, `x^2`, and `x^3` onto comparable scales.

steps.question: On line 25, what reference line does `plt.plot([y_test.min(), y_test.max()], [y_test.min(), y_test.max()])` draw on the `True y` vs. `Predicted y` scatter plot?
steps.answer: It draws the diagonal identity line `Predicted y = True y`, where every point with zero prediction error (`y_pred == y_test`) would lie.

steps.description: Scatter-plot `(y_test, y_pred)`, overlay the diagonal `y = x` line from `y_test.min()` to `y_test.max()`, and display the figure.
